questions: What does RAM do in a computer?
answer: RAM is temporary working memory for programs and data currently in use. It is faster than disk storage, and its contents are lost when the computer turns off.
VRAM is memory used by the GPU. It holds graphics data and GPU workloads such as model weights and intermediate results. It is separate from ordinary system RAM.

questions: How is RAM different from disk storage?
Is RAM the same thing as an SSD?
What is the difference between RAM and storage?
answer: RAM temporarily holds data for running programs. Disk storage keeps files even when power is off. RAM is faster, but it does not replace permanent storage.
The CPU is the main processor. It executes program instructions, performs calculations, and coordinates many tasks on the computer.
A GPU is a processor designed to perform many operations in parallel. It is useful for graphics, matrix calculations, and training or running neural networks.

questions: How does an SSD store files?
answer: An SSD stores files in flash memory and keeps them when power is off. It has no moving parts and is usually faster than a mechanical hard drive.

questions: Why does a computer need an OS?
answer: An operating system manages hardware, memory, files, and running programs. Windows, Linux, and macOS are examples.

questions: What does process mean in computing?
answer: A process is a running instance of a program. It has an identifier and uses resources such as CPU time and memory. One application can have several processes.

questions: How is a thread related to a process?
answer: A thread is a sequence of execution inside a process. Multiple threads can work on different tasks while sharing the process's memory.

questions: Why can a computer become slow?
Explain common reasons for a sluggish PC.
Why might my laptop feel sluggish?
answer: Possible causes include high CPU load, insufficient RAM, slow disk activity, overheating, or a busy application. Check live measurements before deciding which cause applies.

questions: Does high RAM usage prove a memory leak?
Is high memory usage always a leak?
Can I diagnose a memory leak from one reading?
Does memory being nearly full mean a program is leaking?
answer: No. High memory usage alone does not prove a leak. Watch whether one process keeps growing over time under a similar workload, and check whether memory is released when work ends.

questions: What happens when RAM is full?
Why can insufficient memory slow a PC?
How does low available RAM affect performance?
answer: When RAM is insufficient, the operating system may move data to disk through paging. Disk access is slower than RAM, so programs can become less responsive.

questions: Why does the operating system use a page file?
answer: Swap or a page file is disk space used to hold data moved out of RAM. It helps manage memory pressure, but it is slower than RAM.

questions: Why does a program's memory sometimes keep growing?
answer: A memory leak occurs when a program retains memory it no longer needs. Usage can grow over time and eventually reduce available memory or cause failure.

questions: Why can a hot processor run slower?
answer: Thermal throttling reduces a processor's speed to limit temperature. High temperatures and falling clock speeds can indicate throttling, but measurements are needed to confirm it.

questions: How should I interpret CPU utilization?
answer: CPU usage indicates how busy the processor is during a measurement interval. High usage can be normal during demanding work; it does not by itself prove a problem.

questions: Why do programs keep a cache?
answer: A cache stores data that is likely to be needed again, reducing repeated work or slower access. Cached data can often be recreated from its original source.

questions: How does a path identify a file?
answer: A file path identifies a location in the filesystem. An absolute path starts from a root, while a relative path is interpreted from the current directory.
A directory, or folder, groups files and other directories. It helps organize a filesystem and forms part of a file's path.

questions: What belongs in a project's workspace?
answer: A workspace is the set of project folders, files, and settings used for your current work. Its contents depend on the project and the tools you use.
Git tracks changes to files through commits. It helps you review history, work on branches, and combine changes from different versions or contributors.

questions: What does a Git branch do?
answer: A Git branch is a named reference to a line of development. It lets you work on changes separately and later merge them into another branch.

questions: Explain a commit in version control.
answer: A Git commit records a snapshot of tracked changes, along with metadata such as its author and message. Commits form the project's version history.

questions: Explain the Git working tree status.
How can I inspect uncommitted changes?
What information does git status give?
answer: git status shows the current branch and the state of the working tree and staging area. It lists changes such as modified, staged, and untracked files.

questions: What is a Git merge conflict?
Why does Git sometimes need help merging?
answer: A merge conflict occurs when Git cannot combine changes automatically. Review the conflicting content, choose the intended result, and then mark the conflict as resolved.

questions: Does an untracked file belong to a commit yet?
answer: An untracked file exists in the working directory but is not tracked by Git. It will not be included in a commit until you add it to the staging area.

questions: What is a Python virtual environment?
Why use separate environments for Python projects?
answer: A Python virtual environment isolates a project's installed packages. It lets different projects use different dependencies without installing them all into the same environment.

questions: How do programs use environment variables?
answer: An environment variable is a named value passed to a process by its environment. Programs can use it for configuration, such as locating tools or choosing settings.

questions: How does the terminal find commands?
What does PATH tell the operating system?
answer: PATH lists directories searched for executable commands. If a program is not in one of those directories, you may need to use its full path.

questions: Why do machine learning programs use CUDA?
answer: CUDA is NVIDIA's platform for running computations on supported NVIDIA GPUs. Machine learning libraries can use it to accelerate operations such as matrix multiplication.

questions: Does no CUDA mean no GPU?
Can a computer have a GPU without CUDA?
Is a missing CUDA device proof that graphics hardware is absent?
Does CUDA being unavailable mean I have no graphics card?
answer: No. A GPU can exist even when CUDA is unavailable. CUDA needs compatible NVIDIA hardware and software; other GPUs and unsupported installations may not provide it.

questions: What is a GPU out of memory error?
Why can a model run out of VRAM?
What does an out of memory error on the GPU mean?
answer: It means the workload needs more available GPU memory than it can allocate. Reducing batch size or sequence length, or closing another GPU workload, may help.

questions: How is latency different from bandwidth?
answer: Latency is the delay in communication, often measured in milliseconds. Bandwidth is how much data can be transferred per unit of time. A fast connection can still have high latency.

questions: Why does a browser need DNS?
answer: DNS translates domain names into network addresses. If name resolution fails, a browser may be unable to reach a site even when the network connection is working.

questions: Can you tell what tabs are open from a window title?
Does the active window reveal all browser tabs?
Can a foreground title list every tab?
Is a window title enough to know all open tabs?
answer: No. An active window title may identify the foreground application or current page. Listing all browser tabs requires a separate browser observation.

questions: Can you know my current RAM usage without checking?
Do you know my computer's live memory usage from training?
Can model weights tell you which apps are running?
Can you guess my computer's current resources accurately?
answer: No. Current computer state requires a live observation. Training data does not tell me which applications or resources are in use on your machine right now.

questions: Is it safe to close the biggest process?
Should I kill whichever program uses most RAM?
Can I end an unknown process to free memory?
Should I stop a process just because it uses a lot of memory?
answer: First identify the process and whether its work is needed. Closing it may lose unsaved work or interrupt a system task. Memory usage alone is not enough to decide.

questions: Should I delete system files to free space?
Can I remove unknown files in Windows folders?
Is deleting operating system files a good cleanup method?
Can I safely delete unfamiliar system files?
answer: Do not delete unfamiliar system files. Use the operating system's storage cleanup tools and review your own files before removing anything important.

questions: How can I find what is using RAM?
How do I identify memory heavy programs?
Where can I check memory use by application?
How do I see which process uses the most memory?
answer: Inspect the process list and compare memory usage by process. On Windows, Task Manager can show this. Check what each process does before deciding whether to close it.

questions: How can I check disk space?
Where can I see free storage?
How do I inspect available space on a drive?
How do I find how much storage is left?
answer: Inspect the drive's total capacity and free space. On Windows, File Explorer or Storage settings can show this; Robbie's /system command also reports drive space.
